machines.name: deep-research
machines.description: Research a question end to end: decompose it into sub-tasks, dispatch a worker per sub-task, judge whether the answer is complete, then draft and cite a report.

create.description: Start a fresh actor. The response is its id, its state, and the transitions enabled from there.

send.description: The only way to move an actor. Payload keys follow the schema shown for that event. A - in the payload's place reads the JSON from stdin instead.

snapshot.description: Current state and enabled transitions, unchanged. How to orient when handed an id.

describe.description: With an event: that one move — where it leads, what it is for and its schema — and nothing else. Without one: the current state with its full first-arrival instructions, its data and its moves.

state.instructions: State the research question verbatim as you were given it.

targets.description: The question is known; this round needs sub-tasks.

protocol.driving: Every response tells you what you can send next: the states you can reach from here, and under each the event and the payload that must be sent to reach it. Read each one before the next call, and send only an event it lists. A move shown to you whole is named alone on later responses in the same state, until it changes; `node cli.ts --drive describe <actorId> <event.type>` prints it whole again. Every payload passes through your shell, where a quote or apostrophe in free text will eventually break the call before the tool sees it. Pass `-` in the payload's place and feed the JSON on stdin instead — `node cli.ts --drive send <actorId> <event.type> - <<'JSON'`, with the delimiter quoted exactly as shown — and nothing in it is re-parsed.

state.instructions: You are planning round `data.round` of at most `data.maxRounds`. Start broad: a first round maps the ground — which candidates, sources and angles exist — rather than trying to settle the answer, and later rounds add depth aimed at what it turns up. List every sub-task you could commission this round, exhaustively and at least 10: this machine picks which of them run and in what order, so do not trim the list to the ones you would run yourself. Each must be self-contained: a worker sees the research question and its own sub-question, nothing else, and cannot ask you for clarification. State an objective and clear boundaries so two workers do not duplicate each other. Write every boundary in terms the worker can check alone: name the topic it must not cover, never point at another sub-task it cannot see.

What guided fishing trips or kid-friendly charters operate in Branson, MO, including prices, minimum ages and gear provided? Cover only guides and charters, not self-guided fishing.
What are Missouri fishing license requirements for children, including age exemptions, trout permits for Taneycomo, and where to buy them? Cover only licensing and permits.
Which Branson-area fishing species are easiest for kids to catch (bluegill, trout, crappie, catfish) and what seasons, baits and times of year are best? Cover only species and seasons.
Where can families rent boats, fishing gear, or buy bait and tackle in Branson, MO, and which marinas or outfitters (e.g., Lilley's Landing) are kid-friendly? Cover only rentals and supplies.
What do reviews on TripAdvisor, Yelp and travel blogs say about the best places for kids to fish in Branson, MO? Cover only review opinions and rankings.
What safety considerations apply for kids fishing near Branson, such as Taneycomo dam water-release schedules, cold water, and life jacket rules? Cover only safety, not locations.

Are there stocked ponds, trout parks or hatchery attractions near Branson (Shepherd of the Hills Fish Hatchery, Bass Pro Shops, Lake Springfield, Roaring River State Park) good for kids? Cover only these hatchery and stocked-water options.

payload.summary: Lake Taneycomo is a good, beginner-friendly option for kids because MDC stocks about 560,000 rainbow and 15,000 brown trout a year (rainbows are ~90% of the catch), and the lake is fishable year-round. Where you fish matters. The first ~3 miles below Table Rock Dam (to Fall Creek) are artificial lures and flies only, with a 12-20 inch rainbow release slot, and the first 1.5 miles swing between deep fast water during generation and shallow water otherwise, so that stretch is poor for young kids. Below Fall Creek, natural and scented baits (worms, PowerBait) are allowed with no length limit on rainbows, which suits beginners. A trout permit is required to possess trout (daily limit 4); the upper lake and anything upstream of the Hwy 65 bridge also need one. Kid-friendly access: MDC lists covered, accessible public fishing docks at Cooper Creek Access, Rockaway Beach Access (Hwy 176, open 4 AM-10 PM, 417-895-6880) and Empire Electric Park, plus public docks at Branson Lakeside RV Park and along the Branson Landing lakefront. Lilley's Landing Resort & Marina (family-owned since 1982) rents jon boats and pontoons, sells temporary licenses, offers guides, and per a forum poster allows dock fishing for non-guests; its guide Phil Lilley says novices with worms and PowerBait will catch fish. Fall Creek has a pay-to-fish dock per a forum poster, and Fall Creek Marina rents boats with child-size life vests. Below Rockaway Beach the lake shifts to bass, bluegill, redear sunfish and crappie, which MDC calls good for kids and beginners. Short 2-hour beginner/kid guided trips exist but are guide-marketed, with prices from about $325 for 4 hours. Caveats: a forum thread notes kids want steady action and trout fishing can be only fair on some days; MapQuest showed Lilley's as Closed, probably outdated, so confirm. Facts from snippets alone (not read at source): Lilley's details, Fall Creek dock and marina details, guide trip pricing and the 2-hour kids trip, Branson Landing shore-fishing claims. Read in full: the MDC Lake Taneycomo page (docks, stocking, regulations, water conditions).

payload.summary: Table Rock Lake is workable but not an easy kids' lake for bank fishing. Table Rock State Park (read at source: Missouri State Parks page) has a boat ramp near the picnic shelter, fishing allowed 24 hours except in the day-use area (limited hours), bass, crappie and other warm-water species, and fishing supplies at the State Park Marina; the page does not mention fishing docks and only implies bank fishing via a photo caption. Anglers also warn that Table Rock is not really a bank lake and summer bass from shore is hard, with many prime spots boat-only. Indian Point (snippets only) is a Corps of Engineers campground about 4-5 miles from Branson with boat ramps and a swimming beach; no dedicated kids' fishing pier or on-shore fishing rules were confirmed. A Branson.com page notes some resort areas allow shore fishing but to check rules. Licenses (snippets from low-quality affiliate sites, unverified): under-16s generally fish free in Missouri, though a trout permit for youth is disputed; check MDC.
